fundamentals.pe_assessment: Trailing P/E of 20.8x is reasonable for a company growing revenue ~20% YoY in constant currency with expanding margins; forward P/E of 25.2x already prices in the near-term margin drag from the FY26 capex ramp but remains below AMZN's own historical forward-multiple range during prior growth cycles.
fundamentals.margin_analysis: Gross margin 50.3%, operating margin 11.2% (LTM), net margin 10.8%. Management just reported Q2 operating margin expanding to 13.7% from 11.4% a year ago on AWS mix shift and retail logistics efficiency, an improving trajectory.
fundamentals.debt_analysis: Total debt of $153.0B against $411.1B of total equity is a conservative ~37% debt-to-equity for a company this size; an investment-grade balance sheet comfortably supports the announced $220B FY26 capex plan without near-term refinancing risk.
fundamentals.growth_outlook: LTM revenue of $716.9B with AWS posting its fastest growth in 18 quarters and a raised capex outlook aimed at AI/data-center capacity signals management confidence in demand, though free cash flow of only $7.7B (LTM) shows the capex ramp is currently consuming most operating cash flow.
key_risks: Free cash flow compressed to $7.7B against a $220B planned FY26 capex budget — execution/ROI risk on AI infrastructure spend
Forward P/E of 25.2x vs trailing 20.8x prices in continued margin expansion that must be delivered
New Jersey AG antitrust suit over delivery-contractor practices adds legal/regulatory overhang
Insider selling — Bezos filed to sell over $4B of stock under a 10b5-1 plan
key_strengths: AWS delivering its fastest growth in 18 quarters with operating margin expansion (11.4% -> 13.7% YoY)
Q2 results beat the high end of guidance on both revenue and profit
Analyst sentiment strongly positive: 58 of 60 covering analysts rate buy or strong buy, zero sell ratings
Conservative balance sheet (~37% debt/equity) funds growth without near-term dilution or distress
fundamentals.summary: Amazon's fundamentals are strong and improving — AWS-driven margin expansion and a Q2 beat support a buy, though the capex ramp to $220B has temporarily compressed free cash flow and the forward multiple already prices in continued execution.

sentiment.news_summary: News flow is sharply bifurcated: an AWS-driven Q2 beat sent shares up 15-17% to a record high on August 3, but within the same three-week window New Jersey's AG filed an antitrust suit over delivery-contractor practices and Bezos filed to sell over $4B of stock, and the stock has since pulled back roughly 9% from that high.
key_themes: Q2 earnings beat plus raised FY26 capex guidance
notable_headlines: AMZN Stock Soars As AWS AI Boom Ignites Massive Rally (Aug 3, 2026)
New Jersey AG files antitrust suit against Amazon over delivery-contractor practices (Aug 4, 2026)
Bezos files to sell over $4 billion of Amazon stock under Rule 10b5-1 plan (Aug 6, 2026)
What's Going on With Amazon Stock? (Motley Fool, Aug 3, 2026)
sentiment.summary: Sentiment is mixed: a powerful earnings-driven rally has been followed by regulatory and insider-selling headlines plus a technical pullback, leaving no clear directional edge from news flow alone.

technical.trend: Primary uptrend intact (price above SMA-50 and SMA-200) but in a short-term pullback — price sits just below SMA-20 after retreating ~8.75% from the August 3 52-week high of $287.20 following the post-earnings spike.
technical.rsi_assessment: RSI-14 at 33.55 is approaching oversold (<30) but not yet there, reflecting the sharp post-spike cooldown rather than an established downtrend; could resolve as either a dip-buy setup or continued breakdown.
technical.macd_assessment: MACD line (3.16) sits below its signal line (4.63) with a negative and widening histogram (-1.47), confirming bearish short-term momentum even though price remains above the 50/200-day averages.
technical.volume_assessment: Volume ratio of 0.59x (well below the 20-day average) on the recent pullback suggests the decline is a low-conviction cooldown from the post-earnings spike rather than aggressive distribution.
technical.summary: AMZN is in a short-term pullback within an intact longer-term uptrend — bearish MACD momentum and a sub-30-approaching RSI warrant caution, but low volume on the decline and support at the 50/200-day SMAs keep the technical picture balanced rather than outright bearish.

macro.fed_impact: The Fed under new Chair Kevin Warsh held the funds rate at 3.50%-3.75% at both the June and July 2026 meetings; markets have shifted from pricing cuts to acknowledging hike risk given inflation still above target, keeping the cost-of-capital environment tighter than AMZN's aggressive $220B FY26 capex plan would prefer.
macro.interest_rate_outlook: No near-term cut is expected; the next FOMC meeting is September 15-16, 2026. A 'higher for longer' or even hiking-bias stance raises the discount rate applied to Amazon's long-duration AI/data-center capex bets and modestly pressures growth-stock valuations sector-wide.
macro.fx_impact: No AMZN-specific dated FX data is available; USD strength typical of a hawkish-Fed regime would be a mild headwind to AWS/international retail revenue translated back to USD, but this is a general sector effect rather than an AMZN-specific catalyst.
sector_macro_factors: Consumer Cyclical/Internet Retail sector remains sensitive to real consumer spending power, which a higher-for-longer rate regime constrains
Elevated rates raise the opportunity cost of AMZN's $220B capex ramp into AI infrastructure
AWS's enterprise/cloud demand is comparatively rate-insensitive versus AMZN's core retail segment
geopolitical_risks: New Jersey state antitrust suit over delivery-contractor labor practices is a company-specific regulatory risk that could presage similar suits in other states
Broader U.S. antitrust scrutiny of large-cap tech/retail platforms remains an ongoing overhang independent of Fed policy
macro.summary: Macro backdrop is a mild headwind: the Fed is holding rates at 3.50%-3.75% with hike risk rather than cut risk, raising the cost of Amazon's aggressive AI capex plan, though AWS's relative rate-insensitivity partially offsets pressure on the more cyclical retail segment.
